newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer seeks talk show host Jenny Jones' testimony.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer seeks talk show host Jenny Jones' testimony.

text.p: The lead defense attorney of a man accused of gunning down a gay acquaintance after appearing on the "Jenny Jones" daytime talk show said Tuesday he would call the program's host to the stand, despite earlier rulings that Jones does not have to testify.
Attorney James Burdick said testimony from Jones is crucial to the case involving Jonathan Schmitz, 26, of Lake Orion, Michigan.

Schmitz is charged with first-degree murder in the March 9, 1995, shotgun slaying of Scott Amedure, 32, of Orion Township. Three days before the killing, the two men appeared on a taped segment of "The Jenny Jones Show" in which Amedure revealed he had a crush on Schmitz, who says he is not gay.

Defense attorneys argue the show tricked Schmitz into appearing and humiliated him in front of the audience. That, combined with the emotional effects of Graves disease, a thyroid condition from which Schmitz suffers, drove him to commit the crime, they say.

"It's pretty clear you will see me erupt in disbelief and shock if at the conclusion of the people's case the judge doesn't agree Jenny Jones' appearance here at the trial is absolutely mandatory," said Burdick.
Oakland County Circuit Judge Francis O'Brien ruled earlier that Jones is not a relevant witness to Schmitz' defense of diminished mental capacity.

Both prosecutors and defense attorneys asked the Michigan State Court of Appeals to remove Judge O'Brien. The appellate court refused, saying such an action is premature, thus leaving the judge's prior rulings intact.
Questioning of prospective jury members got under way Tuesday, and attorneys said they expect to select a jury of 12 members and three alternatives Thursday.

The jury will have the option of convicting Schmitz of first- or second-degree murder, manslaughter, or reckless discharge causing death. The jury does not have the option of finding Schmitz not guilty.
